The blacklist was drawn up based on tip-offs from citizens in Iran’s southern neighboring countries, as well as Iranian intelligence gathered through field operations and surveillance. 👉 Founded in April 2026 following the US-Israeli invasion, the PGSA was tasked with restricting cargo traffic through the strait. Since, cargo vessels have been able to pass safely only in coordination with the authority. In an attempt to circumvent the restrictions, the US resorted to risky ship-to-ship transfers, with shuttle vessels operating at night, switching off their transponders and disabling their GPS signals for hours at a time. The scheme has also proved costly. The daily charter rate for a Very Large Crude Carrier (VLCC) has surged from $231,400 to more than $1 million. The US must also maintain a military naval presence in the region to oversee the operation. Yet unauthorized tankers keep catching fire in the strait.
